title: How damaging is zero-sum thinking to an agent's interests when the world is positive-sum?
abstract: arXiv:2604.19359v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We study whether zero-sum decision rules, maximin and minimax, harm agents' interests in positive-sum games relative to Nash equilibrium behaviour or, more generally, than best response behaviour. Contrary to an influential evolutionary view, we give illustrations where maximin serves an agent's interests better than Nash equilibrium behaviour. Two new sets of results show that these illustrations are not idiosyncratic. First, for any selected Nash equilibrium in cardinal games, we construct a strategically equivalent game where a maximin profile yields the same pay-offs and we fully characterise when maximin can be made to Pareto dominate that Nash equilibrium and the entire Nash equilibrium set. Second, we show that the relevant Maximin Pareto dominance classes are not knife-edge: they are generically interior, and strict maximin profile dominance occurs on a non-empty open set if and only if a player has at least two actions and t

translated_title: 当世界是正和的时候，零和思维对代理人的利益有多大损害？
translated_abstract: arXiv:2604.19359v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：我们研究了在正和博弈中，相对于纳什均衡行为或更一般的最佳响应行为，零和决策规则（即最大最小化和最小最大化）是否会损害代理人的利益。与一个有影响力的进化观点相反，我们给出了例子，说明在某些情况下，最大化策略比纳什均衡行为更有利于代理人的利益。两组新的结果表明，这些例子并非特例。首先，对于基数博弈中的任意选定的纳什均衡，我们构造了一个策略等价的博弈，在该博弈中，最大化剖面产生相同的收益，并且我们完全刻画了最大化何时能够帕累托支配该纳什均衡以及整个纳什均衡集。其次，我们表明相关的最大化帕累托支配类并非边缘情况：它们通常是内部的，并且严格的极大化剖面支配在非空开集上发生，当且仅当一个玩家至少有两个动作且...
tldr: 本文表明，在正和博弈中，零和决策规则（如最大化策略）在某些情况下反而能比纳什均衡行为更好地服务于代理人的利益，且这一现象具有普遍性而非特例。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that zero-sum decision rules, such as maximin, can sometimes serve an agent's interests better than Nash equilibrium behavior in positive-sum games, and this phenomenon is generic rather than idiosyncratic.
